literal: Is it evening? You are not. Those who united, life-consuming time you are, may you live, O time!
translation: You are not just the evening; you are the life-consuming hour for those who once united. May you prosper, O twilight hour!
modern: பொழுதே! நீ வெறும் மாலைப் பொழுது அல்ல; கூடிப் பிரிந்தவர்களின் உயிரைக் குடிக்கும் கொலைக் காலம் நீ; நீ வாழ்க!
explanation: The heroine, suffering from the pain of separation, addresses the approaching evening. She declares that this hour is not a gentle evening (மாலை) but rather a deadly time (வேலை) that devours the lives of lovers who are separated. The word 'வேலை' primarily means 'time' or 'season', but it also evokes the image of a sharp spear (வேல்) that inflicts a mortal wound. By addressing the evening with the ironic blessing 'வாழி' (may you live), she expresses her deep anguish and resentment toward this painful period of the day.
